title_or_table: Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates (SAIPE), counties, people under 18 in poverty
table_id: SAIPE timeseries, SAEPOVRT0_17_PT, time=2019 and time=2024
geography: Counties and county equivalents in the 50 states and DC
universe_or_base: Related children and other people under 18, under the official poverty measure
unit: counties in each two-point bin of the share of people under 18 in poverty; bin_start and bin_end in percent
vintage: SAIPE 2024 release; 2019 as currently served by the data API
qualification: Each county counts once, whatever its population, so the distributions describe counties, not children, and the note under the chart says so. Model-based estimates under the official poverty measure, which counts pretax cash income and leaves out tax credits such as the child tax credit; the national rate was 16.8 percent in 2019 and 15.5 percent in 2024. County lists differ slightly between years where Connecticut moved from counties to planning regions

bin_start.description: lower edge of the bin, in the bin

bin_end.description: upper edge of the bin, not in the bin

counties.description: counties whose estimate falls in the bin, each counted once

printed_source_line: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates, people under 18 in poverty, 2019 and 2024, counties in the 50 states and DC. Retrieved November 11, 2026. Model-based estimates under the official poverty measure, which leaves out tax credits; counties grouped in two-point bins by Oath & Action.
derivation: For each year, every county with an estimate counted once in the two-point bin, closed on the left, that holds its share of people under 18 in poverty, from 0 to 74 percent, the same edges for both years (the data lead's ruling (g))
notes: 2019: 3141 counties, median 18.70 percent; no estimate: Kalawao County, HI
2024: 3143 counties, median 17.10 percent; no estimate: Kalawao County, HI
